title: Chemical Disasters

source.boundary: Actual Chemical Disasters title left column PDF17/printed35 through references right column PDF23/printed41, above actual Bioterrorism title. Adjacent chapter text excluded.
source.verification: Selected vocabulary and actual title boundaries only; not clinical facts, chemistry, guidance or current treatment validation.

scope: Eighteen selected terms, not exhaustive chapter coverage. Offline vocabulary candidates, not clinical narration, anchors or image-generation prompts. New compositions need not be novel inventions.

source_wording_notes.aerosol: Source has aerosolized and aerosols on printed35; singular headword normalized.
source_wording_notes.personal protective equipment: Exact body phrase on printed38, separate from figure caption.

entries.cue: Familiar household ammonia-cleaner bottle used as a learned cleaning-product token.
entries.reason: Familiar product association, not guaranteed unlabeled bottle recognition. No mixing, handling, exposure or treatment instructions.

entries.cue: Pool-maintenance chemical tub and scoop beside a small swimming pool.
entries.reason: Source itself mentions swimming pools. Not every pool chemical is chlorine; this is a learned contextual token, not chemical identification or safe-use guidance.

entries.cue: Spray can releasing a clearly visible cloud of fine droplets.
entries.reason: Familiar everyday example, not every aerosol source, a particle-size diagram or a claim that all aerosols are visible.

entries.cue: Sugar-cube token visibly dissolving into a clear glass of water.
entries.reason: Everyday property cue, not a claim about any named toxic agent, solubility ranking or safety in water.

entries.cue: A stained mannequin transfers its distinctive stain to an initially clean second mannequin at their point of contact.
entries.reason: Shared stain makes the transfer legible. Metaphor, not a universal route, visibility or exposure-risk rule.

entries.cue: Secret-agent character holding a recognizable branching nerve-wire model.
entries.reason: Agent/spy double meaning avoids forced chemical-name fragments. Not a mechanism, specific agent or clinical syndrome.

entries.cue: Large eye model with a prominent iris surrounding a pupil visibly reduced to a tiny pinhole.
entries.reason: Simple visual state, not a unique cause, diagnostic cutoff or full syndrome.

entries.cue: Eye character shedding conspicuously large tears.
entries.reason: Familiar action can teach the term without a strained pun. Not a specific toxic exposure or emotional cause.

entries.cue: Mannequin mouth with a conspicuous drool trail.
entries.reason: Simple learned category cue, not a severity threshold or diagnosis.

entries.cue: Vivid blue dye in a clear bottle with a large blue droplet.
entries.reason: Partial learned token, not full phonetic recovery or unique dye identification. No drug use, administration or efficacy encoded.

entries.reason: Familiar category cue, not a required protection level, standard or agent-specific equipment specification.

entries.reason: Established removal cue, not a universally appropriate method, fluid, duration or equipment recommendation.
